title: Rate and speed: d = s × t
subject: math
strengths: Most of the class can read 60 km/h as 60 km covered in every hour.
The class can find a distance by multiplying speed by time and check it in parts.

modelAnswers.question: A bus travels at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours. How far does it go? Show the working.
modelAnswers.answer: 150 km: distance = speed × time, so 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

modelAnswers.question: A van travels 120 km in 2 hours. What is its speed?
modelAnswers.answer: 60 km/h: speed = distance ÷ time, so 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h.

commonErrors.misconception: 60 km/h means the bus has travelled 60 km.
commonErrors.example: A learner answers 60 km for the half-hour journey on the worksheet, reading the speed itself as the distance.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: halve the hour first - how far does the bus go in half of one hour at 60 km/h?
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: half the time means half the distance, so in half an hour the bus has gone 30 km, not 60.

commonErrors.misconception: 60 km/h means the bus has travelled 60 km.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner defends 60 km by saying the speed is 60 km/h, so the bus must have travelled 60 km.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say what the 60 in 60 km/h counts - kilometres per hour - then work out the distance for the actual time.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: 60 km/h names a rate, not a total, so after half an hour the bus sits at the 30 km mark, never the 60 km mark.

nextSteps: Reteach speed as distance per hour, landing the same 60 km every hour, before any further rate questions.
Practise building distances in parts - full hours plus a half hour - before landing the multiplication.
